name: Hierocracy
summary: Hierocracy, or papalism, holds that the pope as Christ's vicar has supreme authority over both spiritual and temporal affairs. Secular rulers hold their office from God and are legitimate, but the spiritual power institutes the temporal and may judge, discipline and in the extreme case depose it, while being judged by no one on earth. Law is developed by canonists through the pope's plenitude of power, and submission to the Roman pontiff is held necessary for salvation.
scope: The medieval papal hierocracy of c. 1075-1325: Gregory VII's Dictatus papae, Boniface VIII's Unam sanctam, and the canonists and theologians Hostiensis, Giles of Rome, James of Viterbo and Augustinus Triumphus. It excludes later Catholic rejection of the deposing power, Protestant and Gallican views, dualists such as John of Paris and Dante, and other clerical regimes (Iranian velayat-e faqih, Byzantine caesaropapism). Most questions on economics, technology and modern identity were never addressed, so those answers are low-confidence inferences or neutral.

keyFigures.name: Pope Gregory VII
keyFigures.role: Pope whose Dictatus papae (1075) set out the claim to depose emperors and judge all.

keyFigures.name: Pope Boniface VIII
keyFigures.role: Issued Unam sanctam (1302), the official statement of the two-swords doctrine.

keyFigures.name: Giles of Rome
keyFigures.role: Author of De ecclesiastica potestate (1302), the fullest theoretical defence of papal fullness of power.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Medieval hierocrats wrote about papal jurisdiction, not state medicine; charity was a church task, so no stated view and an honest neutral inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy lies outside the hierocratic texts; just-price and just-wage ideas existed but were not part of the papal supremacy doctrine.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Giles of Rome subordinated property to the church's superior right, and usury was a ground for papal intervention, implying distrust of unregulated markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Giles held that the church has direct lordship over all property and laypeople only use, but this is not state ownership of industry, so the answer is split and inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hierocratic sources do not discuss progressive taxation; nothing in papal supremacy theory points either way.

unions-good.rationale: Trade unions did not exist; guilds were tolerated but the doctrine concerns church and prince, so no position can be derived.

property-fundamental.rationale: Giles argued the church holds superior direct dominion over all property and can recover goods misused, so property is not fundamental against church authority.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations as a modern issue were never addressed; guild and trade regulation by authority fits the general outlook but is inferred only.

cut-welfare.rationale: Care for the poor was a church duty and a prince's obligation under clerical guidance, so cutting relief fits poorly; inferred from Christian charity rather than stated.

worker-ownership.rationale: Property was held under hierarchical lordship subject to the church, not by workers collectively; inferred from Giles on dominion.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the church did run inquisitions later, but the hierocratic texts discuss jurisdiction, not security surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic question with no hierocratic position; moral regulation by the church would favour restriction but this is thin inference.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; blasphemy and heresy would be restricted but hate speech toward groups as such is a modern category.

strong-leader.rationale: The papal monarchy of Dictatus Papae favours concentrated authority in one head, but the statement concerns a secular leader bypassing gridlock, which hierocrats would subject to the pope.

state-harmful.rationale: Unam Sanctam says the temporal sword is a real power wielded for the church; temporal authority is necessary and ordained by God, never harmful in itself.

limit-guns.rationale: The doctrine concerns who commands the temporal sword, not who may own arms privately, so there is no stated position and adherents could go either way.

empower-police-military.rationale: The temporal sword is to be used at the priest's bidding, so coercive power is legitimate, but funding levels are not discussed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Church moral authority would condemn it; inferred from canon-law morality, not a stated position in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Dictatus Papae centralizes appeals, legates, councils and appointments in Rome, favouring universal jurisdiction over local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penance and correction featured in church thought, but prison policy is not discussed; split.

traditional-family.rationale: Canonists governed marriage as a sacrament and church jurisdiction, so the church backed the family as a foundation, though this is not the core of hierocracy.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Canon law, the legal tool of hierocracy, treated marriage as a sacrament between man and woman; an adherent would strongly oppose it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Church moral teaching enforced through canon law forbade abortion; hierocrats claim authority over such moral law, so strongly disagree.

more-religion-public.rationale: Unam Sanctam makes spiritual authority superior to temporal power and subjection to the pope necessary for salvation, so public life should be ordered by religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Modern question absent from medieval sources; no hierocratic position can be derived.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Medieval canonists assumed a fixed natural and divinely ordered sex difference; inferred and anachronistic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Hierocrats thought in terms of one universal Christian community under the pope, not national cultures, so the answer is split.

gradual-change.rationale: Dictatus Papae stresses that the Roman church never erred and its rulings stand unless the pope revokes them, favouring established order, but reform (Gregorian) was radical.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The universal Christian community under the pope has no border policy in the texts; a Christian-only entry rule is possible but not documented, so the answer is neutral.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The papacy claimed a universal jurisdiction over Christendom, which resembles supranational authority, but UN-style bodies are modern and secular.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; usury was policed but trade policy was not part of the doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Dictatus Papae holds that only the pope may be called universal and that princes answer to him; a single Christian commonwealth outranks national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Just-war and crusade ideas existed under papal authority, but human-rights intervention is modern; split.

open-borders.rationale: Hierocracy imagines one Christian commonwealth under the pontiff but with princes ruling distinct realms, so borders persist; inferred from that structure.

limit-growth.rationale: Medieval hierocratic writing has no concept of economic growth, so nothing can be inferred about limiting it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate change is entirely outside the medieval canonists' horizon, and no principle of papal supremacy decides it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Salvation is spiritual and attained through the church, not technology; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is anachronistic for a doctrine of 1075-1325; no principle of papal supremacy bears on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Hierocrats allowed the pope to depose heretical or tyrannical princes, but lay revolution from below was not licensed; resistance was legitimate only through papal authority.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority belongs to the clerical hierarchy and canonists, which resembles rule by trained experts, though they are clergy not policy experts.

central-planning.rationale: Giles of Rome had temporal affairs left to princes with only occasional papal intervention, which fits poorly with comprehensive economic planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Giles gives the church superior dominion over property but nothing on worker or public enterprise, so this stays neutral.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single land tax is a modern fiscal proposal with no counterpart in hierocratic texts.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hierocratic texts do not address inheritance taxation; hereditary lordship was accepted but its taxation is not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Relief of the poor was a church and prince duty tied to charity, not an unconditional state payment; inferred against.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection is not part of papal supremacy theory and medieval trade regulation was local.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Hierocrats said temporal affairs are left to princes and the church intervenes only on spiritual grounds like usury, so strategic state investment has little support; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Giles gives the church direct lordship over property with laypeople using it, and says nothing on distribution among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not discussed; medieval society was monetary and the church held property, so abolition is inferred as rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banks did not exist; the doctrine's only monetary concern is the usury ban, which does not settle this.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; guild orders fit a hierarchical society but are outside the doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: The church claims one ruling spiritual authority, but party rule is a modern form; inferred disagreement as a secular party would stand under the pope.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hierocrats held that princes' offices were ordained by God and legitimate, though subject to papal judgment; the pope himself is an elective monarch.

democracy-best.rationale: Authority descends from God through the pope, not from voters; anachronistic and inferred from the descending theory of power.

direct-votes.rationale: Authority is hierarchical and descending, so legislation by popular vote has no basis; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power rests on the clerical hierarchy, not workers; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: The pope claims universal jurisdiction over Christendom, which tells against dividing it, but secession as such is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Giles argued that spiritual power precedes and outranks the temporal and that priests institute kings, treating clerical rulers as fitted to judge.

political-violence-never.rationale: Unam Sanctam says the temporal sword is wielded for the church at the priest's will, affirming coercive force under religious authority.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; crusade ideals are different from this claim.

separate-church-state.rationale: Unam Sanctam declares that one sword must be subordinated to the other and the temporal subjected to the spiritual, rejecting strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hierocracy was elaborated by canonists with the plenitude of power, so law rests on canon law and scriptural claims rather than scripture alone.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The temporal sword is held by the church and used at its bidding, so justice and arms belong to authority under the hierarchy, not firms.

military-superiority.rationale: The temporal sword is held for the church, but superiority over rival powers is not discussed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The pope is universal head of one Christian community; the claim of an ethnic nation does not appear, inferred disagreement.

class-struggle-history.rationale: History is ordered by divinely instituted authority and salvation under the church, not class conflict; Marxian claim is foreign to the doctrine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The hierarchy of spiritual over temporal and of clergy over laity conflicts with equalizing outcomes; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Giles held unbelievers are not true owners, but modern indigenous claims are not addressed; low confidence.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations for colonialism is a modern claim; the sources give no basis for a view.

civilizational-union.rationale: The hierocratic ideal is one Christian community subject to the Roman pontiff, uniting nations under shared faith.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Giles made lordship depend on justice and fealty to God, not self-interest; selfishness is sin.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Subjection of every creature to the pontiff is described as necessary for salvation, putting obedience to a spiritual order before individual claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Medieval hierocratic texts do not discuss the intrinsic value of nature.

limit-population.rationale: Church teaching on procreation; inferred and not discussed in the sources.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrial civilization postdates the doctrine; no position can be derived.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on order and established institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; church moral authority would restrain it by inference.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Authority rests on the priestly office as God's vicar, so algorithmic rule has no place; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic technology question with no hierocratic content.

restore-past-order.rationale: Gregorian reformers presented their claims as restoring the ancient order of the church, but they also innovated; a defensible split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy is judged by conformity to the church's spiritual law and salvation, not results alone.

direct-action.rationale: Action against rulers goes through papal sentences such as excommunication and deposition, not direct popular action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Unam Sanctam endorses coercive means under church command, but a general rule that means mirror ends is not stated.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred rejection; entirely foreign to the doctrine.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Giles distinguishes priests, kings and subjects with different offices, so a differentiated social order is basic.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Almsgiving is a church duty but distribution by need as an economic principle is absent from the doctrine.

production-for-use.rationale: The question of production for profit versus use is not discussed by hierocratic writers apart from usury.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Unaddressed; condemnation of usury exists, but profit as exploitation is a Marxian thesis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Power belongs to the spiritual hierarchy, so class dictatorship is rejected.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from manorial and church landholding with no collective ideal.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist claim foreign to hierocratic thought, which saw war as a matter of just cause and papal authority; inferred disagreement.

taxation-theft.rationale: Giles gave church direct dominion over property and hierarchy rights to levy, so taxation is not theft; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: The spiritual power judges the temporal for sin and moral failure, so state restriction extends beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The doctrine locates rights in an order of offices under the pope and the church, not in individuals.

conscription.rationale: The temporal sword is used at the priest's command, which implies rulers may raise force, but conscription is not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Dictatus Papae says whoever is not at peace with the Roman church is not Catholic, so exit is not valued.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is an instrument of a sacred order, not a firm; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberty in the modern sense is not a hierocratic category; the doctrine concerns obedience and salvation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Universities existed in the period but the hierocrats made no claim about their power over rulers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Anachronistic; universal Christian community implies no racial ranking.

organic-representation.rationale: Hierocracy sees society as ordered estates under clergy, close to organic orders, but representation as such is not discussed.

total-state.rationale: Hierocrats held the pope should not ordinarily exercise temporal power directly and that princes handle temporal affairs, so not a total state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Hierocracy concerns a universal church and not national decadence and rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Crusading was papal but the doctrine addresses jurisdiction, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Dictatus Papae lets the pope release subjects from oaths of fealty to wicked rulers, accepting feudal oaths but placing them under papal judgment.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed by hierocratic texts; serfdom existed in the period.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Hierocrats held that truth is given by the church and revelation; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: The doctrine rests on universal spiritual and moral law judged by the Roman pontiff for all humans.

single-common-good.rationale: A single end, salvation, is guided by the church for all, with temporal government subordinate to it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; medieval hierocrats said nothing about a modern Jewish state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not discussed in the sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: The church used Latin as a universal language; reviving national languages is not part of the doctrine.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Dictatus Papae shows a strictly hierarchical order in which the pope appoints and deposes, which tells against voting in firms; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was run by the church, but voucher schemes are modern and not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Deficit policy is anachronistic for the period and the doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred; property subordinate to church claims.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; clergy as moral guides, but the doctrine relies on law and sanctions.

national-self-determination.rationale: The pope claims universal authority over princes, so each nation's self-rule is conditional.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; papal authorisation was the analogue.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Subjection to the pontiff is a matter of faith necessary for salvation, so faith rather than reason alone guides.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The doctrine is addressed to every human creature, so excluding non-citizens from relief sits poorly with it; inferred from the universalism of Unam Sanctam.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; adherents' views on work and charity vary.

class-collaboration.rationale: Estates cooperating under clerical guidance; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The church preserved libraries and learning; inferred rejection of destroying cultural institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: A third-world front of dominated nations is a modern idea outside the doctrine.

workers-nation.rationale: Hierocracy divides society into clergy, princes and subjects under one head, not working classes organised by nation; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Medieval canon law reflected distinct roles; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is among the grounds Giles lists for papal intervention in temporal matters, supporting legal prohibition.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Unam Sanctam claims all human creatures are subject to the pontiff, which does not fit legal racial separation; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The temporal power is instituted by God and the spiritual power, not an instrument of a class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the doctrine.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Assimilation policy is not discussed; conversion rather than cultural assimilation would matter to a hierocrat.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy claim with no source in hierocratic thought; inferred rejection.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems for legislatures are not part of the hierocratic doctrine.

national-mission.rationale: Hierocrats claim a mission for the church, not a country.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The clerical hierarchy in Dictatus Papae is male and accepted as divinely ordered, so a critique of structural patriarchy is not shared; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Giles said corrupt princes may be judged, but not a generic claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is modern, and church teaching on marriage and procreation would oppose state prevention; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for state killings is modern; hierocrats held the pope is judged by no one, but this concerns rulers' forces generally.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The church supervises temporal power and spiritual ends, which exceeds a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The doctrine's universal community of all human creatures gives no basis for racial discouragement of marriage; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: All human creatures are subject to the pontiff, implying shared status as souls, but offices are ranked.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate outside the doctrine.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Canonists maintained separate ecclesiastical jurisdiction over clergy and marriage; a uniform lay code is opposed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Giles names heresy as grounds for papal intervention, so leaving the church would be restricted; inferred, though conversion into it was encouraged.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu nationalist demand with no Christian basis; inferred rejection.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion shapes society; schools under church supervision; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis with no counterpart in hierocracy.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Giles derives rule from church institution and fealty to God, not the governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not part of hierocratic texts.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced expulsions of minorities are not discussed in the doctrine, though Jews and heretics were expelled by princes at times.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The temporal sword may be used at the church's command, so initiating force is permissible when authorised.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Giles grounded lordship in justice and fealty rather than struggle; inferred disagreement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Parties are anachronistic, though the church did punish heresy; neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Pope declared unbound by earthly law, which is the arbitrary power the statement criticizes; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Giles' fullness of power places spiritual and temporal in one source, rejecting checks between co-equal bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: The doctrine places leadership in a priestly hierarchy, not a revolutionary party; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Care for the poor was a Christian duty of rulers and church; inferred, not stated in the supremacy texts.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are outside the medieval doctrine.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Church teaching saw poverty as a moral and charity matter rather than a demographic one; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: A Christian commonwealth under one pope stresses unity of faith, but ethnic diversity as such is not discussed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred; offices by appointment by the pope.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Giles allowed the pope to act outside ordinary law for any cause he deems sufficient, which is a model of emergency prerogative.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The just-price tradition existed, but papal supremacy texts do not discuss grain price caps.

party-controls-media.rationale: Media were not a concern; the church controlled books but through ecclesiastical, not party, authority.

party-commands-army.rationale: The temporal sword is wielded at the priest's bidding; party command of an army has no place in the doctrine.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay rules for representatives are modern and not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The pope claimed supranational authority but EU is secular.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Heads of state command forces but under the pope's direction.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Dictatus Papae places the church under pope, legates and bishops, deposable by the pope, not congregations or assemblies.

clerical-rule.rationale: Unam Sanctam says the spiritual power must institute and judge the earthly power, with the pope as supreme.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Hierocrats thought subjects owe obedience to rulers unless the pope releases them, so working for one's own government's defeat is rejected; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Giles names sacrilege and heresy as grounds for intervention, supporting church supervision of morals and writings; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: The pope may depose bishops and absolve subjects of fealty, a recall by a higher authority, not voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances and bases are modern topics.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Church and lords held land with tenants using it, so abolishing rent conflicts with the property order described by Giles; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The temporal sword is kept by rulers and used at the church's command, not by a citizen militia; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources on papal supremacy say nothing about town versus country life, and monastic ideals cut both ways.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside the doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The clergy were the educated class, so hierocrats would not hold this; but there is no documented view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Unam Sanctam says submission to the Roman pontiff is necessary for salvation, so cultures without the faith are not equal; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The sword is used by the church's authority; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Church moral teaching on sex and gender would oppose it; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The creation account was part of the church's teaching; inferred though the debate is modern.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Church moral authority over public morals fits restriction; inferred from the moral supervision hierocrats claimed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules did not exist in the form asked, and the doctrine defines membership by baptism and not descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not discussed; Latin served as the church's common language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The doctrine requires all to submit to one authority, so exemptions for other religions would not be granted; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Dictatus Papae says those not at peace with the Roman church are not Catholic, which values conformity; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A decolonisation claim outside the doctrine.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making by elected assembly conflicts with authority descending from the pope; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Growth is not a hierocratic aim, so no view exists.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Christian almsgiving as a duty suggests support for aid; inferred from charity not stated in sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are far outside the period, and no principle of papal supremacy settles the question.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Heads of state are not chosen by popular vote under hierocracy; popes are elected by cardinals, and princes inherit.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking postdates the doctrine, whose only monetary concern is the usury ban.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The papacy claimed lands under the Donation of Constantine, but peace-for-land trades are not discussed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Giles made dominion conditional on justice and church oversight, so property is justified in service of a higher good and can be recovered when misused.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate outside the doctrine.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is modern and unrelated to the supremacy claims of the papalist canonists.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations are not discussed, though crusading coalitions under papal call existed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources discuss papal judgment of princes, not the legality of annexations by consent of peoples.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Unam Sanctam asserts the opposite: the temporal power is subjected to the spiritual and judged by it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Parties were absent; the pope stands above princes but is not nonpartisan symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Hierocratic writers did not discuss regional secession from a state, only the pope's authority over princes.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country two systems is modern and outside the doctrine.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hierocrats said princes' office was ordained by God but they were subject to the pope; divine descent of rulers is not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income taxation did not exist in the medieval period, so the doctrine has no view on its rate structure.

character-from-environment.rationale: Christian anthropology of sin and grace stresses innate nature and the soul; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Giles held the pope is bound by no earthly law and may act outside ordinary law, though bound by divine law, so the supreme ruler is unbound by positive law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space travel is outside the horizon of medieval papalism, and nothing in the doctrine bears on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The pope holds the fullness of power and the church is an internal monarchy; a mixed constitution is not the model.

leader-cult.rationale: Dictatus Papae claims his is the only name spoken in churches, which sits near honours for one leader, but the statement concerns a national leader.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question with no hierocratic content.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property rests under church dominion; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: A modern question about expelled populations, not addressed in the papalist texts.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims by nationality are outside the doctrine, which grounds claims in the pope's rights.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Giles lists heresy as ground for papal intervention and unbelievers are not true owners, supporting legal penalties for leaving the faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress law is not discussed by hierocratic writers.

common-currency.rationale: Shared currencies between states are not discussed in the sources on hierocracy.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union rests on the shared Christian faith under the pontiff rather than ancestry and language; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural institutions are a modern nationalities question absent from the doctrine.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A debate among modern minorities, with no counterpart in the papalist texts.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: History is seen through providential spiritual order.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is modern; the nearest medieval concern is just price and usury, which is not about cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are modern and are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Dictatus Papae makes the pope's judgment final over lay authorities, so courts are not bound to any majority; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The all-male hierarchy of pope, legates and bishops is the model, so quotas conflict; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic economic blocs are modern and not discussed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are modern and the doctrine has no view on them.

moral-incentives.rationale: Christian moral formation and salvation as motives fits this; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Hierocrats allowed removal of rulers only by papal sentence, not by small armed groups; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierocrats accepted hereditary princes and nobles while subjecting them to papal judgment.

history-own-civilization.rationale: A Christendom-centred view of history follows from the claim that all must submit to the Roman pontiff; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Giles denied that unbelievers hold true lordship, which licenses rule over them by the faithful.

patriotic-education.rationale: Hierocrats favour loyalty to the church rather than to a nation, so this is split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Modern American debate with no hierocratic content.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation by banks or a public body is a modern question; only usury is addressed by the doctrine.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A debate within Marxism and economics, not touched by the medieval papalists.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Influence over former imperial regions is a modern foreign-policy question outside the doctrine.

delink-world-market.rationale: A dependency-theory proposal with no counterpart in hierocratic writing.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept outside the doctrine.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The doctrine asserts a hierarchy with legal claims over private conduct, which does not fit absolute private freedom; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Giles' view that the pope is bound by no human law and judged by God alone conflicts with entrenched human limits.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders are a modern topic, not addressed by the papalist canonists.

elective-rulers.rationale: The pope is elected, but hierocrats accepted hereditary princes; Innocent IV allowed papal choice of a monarch when a throne is vacant.

minority-veto.rationale: Dictatus Papae says the pope alone makes laws and judges all, binding dissenters.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The papal deposing power allowed removal of rulers for heresy or extreme misgovernment, though through the pope not by subjects acting alone.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Supreme lawmaking authority sits with the pope.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Giles ties lordship to justice and fealty, implying duties of the powerful; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Clergy are to actively order the temporal; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mass media did not exist; the claim comes from modern critical theory, not hierocracy.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian concept outside the doctrine.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim outside the doctrine.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources discuss papal control of church offices, not birth requirements for state posts.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist question outside the doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development policy is outside the period and the doctrine of papal supremacy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Claims to lost territory are not discussed in the sources, apart from papal claims under the Donation of Constantine.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Giles denies unbelievers true lordship, which cuts against such claims for non-Christians, but the question is modern.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism postdates the doctrine, so there is no hierocratic position on constitutional anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Twentieth-century comparisons of regimes are anachronistic for the medieval doctrine.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A question of American history with no connection to medieval papalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Public memorial controversy is modern and not addressed in hierocratic texts.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Modern social-policy debate outside the doctrine of papal supremacy.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Modern social-policy debate outside the doctrine of papal supremacy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Unam Sanctam presents one universal order under the pontiff for all humans, against civilisational pluralism; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The temporal sword is held under the church's command, but a political role for armies is not discussed.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wage recognition for domestic work is modern and not addressed.

filial-duty.rationale: Church teaching on honouring parents fits this; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Company takeovers are modern and not addressed in the hierocratic sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Canonists administered marriage law and treated marriage as indissoluble, so ending a marriage at will conflicts with that law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The pope can depose bishops but only from above; recall by those below is not the model.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension funds are modern, so the doctrine gives no view.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Giles' direct dominion approximates it but with the church not the community.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Giles' pope is bound by no earthly law, so a parliament's control of the purse is unlikely; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Latin as church language, but not a state-language doctrine.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Alien landholding is not discussed in the texts on papal supremacy.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern anti-discrimination doctrine with no counterpart in the papalist writings.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Christian asceticism critique of wealth and status; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Papal support of rival claimants existed but arming insurgents is not discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The pope claimed to judge princes anywhere, but great-power troop moves in allied lands are not discussed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign money are modern, so there is no stated hierocratic position.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs and universities is a modern issue not found in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The sources do not discuss family subsidies, though church teaching favoured large families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchase are modern and not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: State employment of last resort is modern, so the papalist texts give no basis for a view.

democratic-peace.rationale: A modern international-relations claim; hierocrats did not consider democracies.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Subjection is necessary for salvation; Dictatus Papae calls for obedience, so a general duty to obey rightful authority exists.

non-intervention.rationale: The pope may judge and depose foreign princes, rejecting non-interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Industrial unions are a modern form; the doctrine does not address labour organisation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, though medieval church and princes sometimes made such charges.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage was a sacrament governed by canon law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Giles' pope acts outside ordinary law for any cause he sees fit, which favours discretion over public access; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is modern and not addressed by the doctrine.

informal-organisation.rationale: Only the pope may create new congregations and law, so autonomous small groups are not the model; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Dictatus Papae makes the pope the judge of princes and universal, so higher law outranks national constitutions.

religious-nation.rationale: Christendom as a community bound by faith under the pope; inferred for a nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Dictatus Papae says all princes must kiss the pope's feet, a ritual deference to the leading authority.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is modern and the papalist texts say nothing on it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The church held that private use of property is accepted, but production by common ownership is not discussed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism postdates the doctrine, and papal supremacy theory gives no stated position.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are modern, so the doctrine gives no guidance.

religion-illusion.rationale: Unam Sanctam makes the church and subjection to the pontiff necessary for salvation, treating religion as true.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A Marxist historical judgment with no hierocratic counterpart.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A modern feminist-socialist claim not addressed in the medieval texts.

socialized-care.rationale: Care of children and homes was seen as a family matter under church moral guidance; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is a modern nationalist concern, not found in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with indigenous nations are modern, so no hierocratic position is documented.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not discussed in the doctrine, though monasteries held property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policies in minority regions are modern and absent from the doctrine.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A twentieth-century third-way slogan with no hierocratic counterpart.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Papal claim to lands via the Donation of Constantine.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No hierocratic basis exists for the claim; inferred rejection by any adherent.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Canon law, the tool of hierocracy, condemned same-sex acts, and secular punishment fits the claim that church morals bind rulers; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Heresy named as ground for papal intervention supports suppression of religious dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Giles names sacrilege and heresy as grounds for papal intervention in temporal matters, so civil punishment of false worship is endorsed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The medieval texts do not discuss overseas colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic concept; the closest hierocratic analogue is crusading under papal call, which is not the same claim.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The pope could declare a heretical ruler deposed and release subjects from allegiance, although by papal sentence not by private force.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Dictatus Papae gives all power of appointment to the pope; broad participation is not the model.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A modern academic concept with no counterpart in medieval papalism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Church teaching on sex would oppose legal recognition; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Canon law enforced church moral doctrine that life is God's gift, so assisted killing would be opposed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The left-right axis postdates the doctrine, so there is no stated view.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to the papalist texts.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Giles denies unbelievers true lordship, but the question of Islam and Western values is modern.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Unam Sanctam says all power is ordained by God and flows through the spiritual power that institutes the earthly.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Public religion is encouraged by the doctrine, so dress bans are opposed; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace legal protections are modern and not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: A twentieth-century economic model not discussed in medieval texts.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Unam Sanctam affirms the temporal sword as a real power wielded for the church, so abolition is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: A developmental policy slogan outside the period of the doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Cold War bloc neutrality is modern and the papalist texts do not address it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hierocrats accepted hereditary princes while claiming judgment over them.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Usury prohibition is stated but mutual banks are not.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Lender conditionality is modern and not addressed in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Voting was not the basis of authority, so franchise rules are not discussed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim not addressed by the papalists.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept outside the doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Printing did not exist and the claim comes from modern radical thought.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Giles' pope is a creature without halter or bridle who may act outside ordinary law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The universal claim over all human creatures conflicts with a racial franchise; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is modern and not addressed.

open-government-data.rationale: Open records are modern; the sources describe a papal power acting at its own discretion.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Canonists governed marriage and the church restricted marriage with non-Christians; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Consumer boycotts of minority shops are not discussed in the sources on papal supremacy.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Authority descends from the pope; random assemblies deciding laws conflict with that; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Dictatus Papae says the Roman church has never erred and never will, resisting reinterpretation by others.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The papalist texts do not link wealth concentration to liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Canon law morality treated same-sex acts as sinful, so an adherent would likely oppose open service, though the military question is modern.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Unam Sanctam makes subjection to the pontiff necessary for salvation, opposing state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The temporal sword is legitimate coercion, and the church has its own prisons, so abolition is rejected; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Authority is hierarchical and unified under the pope, so mandatory sharing between communities is not the model; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Church charity was central, but hierocrats also expect princes to act under church guidance, so this is split.

term-limits.rationale: Not discussed; the pope serves for life.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is modern and unconnected to the doctrine.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is a modern concern not found in the medieval texts.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The clerical hierarchy of the pope, legates and bishops was male only.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Medieval canon law assumed a husband's headship; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Local voting by foreign residents is a modern question not addressed.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are modern and the doctrine gives no stated view.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyright are modern, so there is no hierocratic position.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are a twentieth-century phenomenon outside the doctrine.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is modern and unrelated to medieval papalism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are a modern question the papalist texts do not address.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition is a modern legal and memory question not addressed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Giles speaks of lordship, not of income from property versus work, so there is no stated view.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Unam Sanctam affirms the temporal sword; just force is lawful, so a ban on killing in defence is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National continuity myths are modern and not part of the doctrine.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Church teaching treats sex as given by nature and God; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Church teaching treats the categories as fixed; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The church honours martyrs as saints, but this is for the faith and not the nation; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The temporal order is judged by the spiritual power and is directed to salvation.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A diaspora nationalist question that medieval papalism does not address.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural nationalism is modern and the texts do not address it.

god-not-male.rationale: Traditional Christian God-language is male; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Dictatus Papae says no chapter or book is canonical without papal authority, which excludes this test; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic nationalism is modern and absent from the sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: A modern national-unity demand not addressed by the doctrine.

independent-unions.rationale: Trade unions are modern and the papalist texts do not address them.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The doctrine locates power in a clerical hierarchy and not workers; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal utilities are modern and the texts give no view.

second-chamber.rationale: Bicameral legislatures are modern; the papalists described no legislature.

municipal-property.rationale: Giles puts direct dominion over property with the church, not communities; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Dictatus Papae centralizes appeals, councils and appointments in Rome, opposing confederation of free towns.

family-wage.rationale: The medieval just-wage idea supports it; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is modern and unrelated to the doctrine.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is modern and the sources say nothing on it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital cash privacy is a modern question with no counterpart in the doctrine.

online-anonymity.rationale: Internet anonymity is modern and not addressed.

person-over-state.rationale: Hierocrats value persons as souls, but also hold the temporal power must serve spiritual ends; split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The doctrine rests on the claim that humans have a spiritual end served by the church, with temporal government subordinate.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Dictatus Papae shows central authority revoking and transferring local offices.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is modern, with no stated hierocratic position.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is modern and not discussed in the sources.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not discussed in the papalist texts, which stress a faith-based community.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Crusades were offensive in some respects; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The community is defined by faith under the pontiff, not by language; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates are modern; the papalist texts propose no electoral scheme.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A modern nationalist claim not found in the sources.

free-public-college.rationale: University tuition policy is modern and not addressed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pollution pricing is modern and unrelated to the doctrine.

future-generations.rationale: The sources do not discuss duties to future generations in an environmental sense.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not discuss women's distinct values in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms limitation is modern; the sources only affirm the temporal sword.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Giles' pope acts freely outside ordinary rules, so enforced openness conflicts; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Cross-border capital flows are modern, so there is no hierocratic view.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Armed force is held by princes under the church; the doctrine does not discuss monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The temporal sword is used at the priest's bidding, so refusal conflicts unless the war is unjust; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage bargaining between unions and employers is modern and not addressed.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are a modern welfare device not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal borrowing limits are modern and unrelated to the doctrine.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: A twentieth-century development demand outside the doctrine.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Temporal power is ordained and instituted by the spiritual power, so smashing it is not endorsed; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The doctrine asserts one order for all; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is modern and not addressed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Hierocrats hold the church, not the nation, as sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are modern, so nothing in the doctrine bears on them.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A modern theory of regional exploitation absent from the texts.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Every human creature is declared subject to the Roman pontiff, assuming a common nature and end.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is modern and unrelated to the doctrine.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Unam Sanctam declares that submission to the Roman pontiff is necessary for salvation and that there is one holy Catholic church outside which there is no salvation.

farm-price-support.rationale: Hierocratic texts concern papal jurisdiction, not agricultural policy; the church's just-price ideas give no clear verdict.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine says nothing on weapons policy beyond papal authority over the temporal sword.

workers-own-party.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the hierarchical, corporate medieval order and papal claim to supervise all temporal powers, which leaves no place for class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the canonist view that church and law may judge harmful acts and the Christian view of the body as God's creation.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; medieval canonists worked within a patriarchal order of custom, so equal inheritance is inferred to be foreign to the doctrine.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The papal hierocracy was universal and Latin-based; the question of vernacular naming was outside it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; canon law knew remedies for harm to neighbours but no view on pollution regulation is documented.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The doctrine places lawmaking in the pope's plenitude of power, while accepting that temporal rulers act under custom; no stated view on advisory chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position on environmental protection versus liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; canonists valued both fixed canons and equitable discretion, so no clear inference.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anachronistic; a universal church spanning many tongues had no doctrine on migrants' language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Medieval hierocrats never addressed trade unions or closed shops, so this is a neutral inference.

voter-id.rationale: Papal theory had no mass elections or citizenship checks to regulate; no view can be inferred beyond neutrality.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Unam Sanctam holds that submission to the Roman pontiff is necessary for salvation, so no rival interpretation could stand level with the pope's in law.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The spiritual power institutes and may depose the temporal ruler, so legitimacy comes from the pope and God, not from electoral choice and removal of rulers.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from canon law, which condemned fornication and confined sex to marriage; the sources cover jurisdiction, not sexual morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; the hierocrats supported papal control of order and doctrine but said nothing about communications networks.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare was a church task and cash-transfer schemes were never discussed, so a neutral inference.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from a clerical, hierarchical order in which public authority was not conceived as open to women by right of equality; the sources do not discuss it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the claim that the church is Christ's own institution and the guide to moral order, so adherents would reject blaming it for oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: The medieval theorists had no modern concept of race, so no stated view; adherents would neither affirm nor deny it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from a view of the church as the proper guide to family and moral order; state ministries for gender equality would be foreign to it.

missingStatements.text: The pope should have the power to depose a ruler and release that ruler's subjects from their allegiance.
missingStatements.rationale: Dictatus papae claims that the pope may depose emperors and release subjects from fealty to wicked rulers, and the deposing power was later exercised against Henry IV.

missingStatements.text: The highest religious authority should be able to judge the rulers of states, and no earthly authority may judge it in return.
missingStatements.rationale: Unam sanctam says the spiritual power judges the temporal while the highest power can be judged by God alone, and Dictatus papae says no one may judge the pope.

missingStatements.text: Religious authority holds the superior right over all property, and laypeople hold it only by use and on condition of just conduct.
missingStatements.rationale: Giles of Rome argued the church has direct dominion over all property and can recover goods misused, a distinctive hierocratic claim no statement captures.
missingStatements.declined: Giles of Rome's dominion thesis is idiosyncratic to medieval canon-law writers; property-serves-common-good covers the modern contested question.

notes: Hierocracy is strongest on church-state, authority and law statements; most economic and modern-identity statements are neutral or low-confidence inferences because the doctrine was a medieval jurisdictional theory. Dualists like John of Paris and Dante, and later Catholic theologians such as Bellarmine and Suarez, rejected the full claim.
